title: No combat (D-1)
engineBehaviour: D-1: MOVE_PIECES into a system with enemy units is accepted and nothing else happens; the system is shown as contested. No tactic cards, dice, damage, retreat or battle results (activation step 4 is skipped).
officialBehaviour: Moving units into a system with opposing units in the same theater starts a combat resolved in combat rounds with dice and tactic cards (RR p.2 step 4, RR p.4-5, LTP p.14-15).
followUp: Combat slice: implement RR p.4-5 including retreat and winning a battle; replace the contested state.

title: No missions; Assignment Phase is empty (D-2, R-2)
engineBehaviour: D-2: the Assignment Phase passes automatically with an event; a Command Phase turn is only ACTIVATE_SYSTEM or PASS; there is no opposition to missions.
officialBehaviour: Leaders are assigned to facedown missions (Rebels first), and a Command Phase turn may reveal a mission that can be opposed with dice (RR p.3, p.8-9, LTP p.6-8).
followUp: Missions slice: hands, mission decks, starting missions, assignment, reveal and opposition; then mission effects (loyalty, capture, new base, projects).

title: Incomplete Refresh Phase (D-3, R-7)
engineBehaviour: R-7 / D-3: Refresh runs only step 1 (all leaders return, LEADERS_RETURNED) and the +1 time advance of step 5 (TIME_ADVANCED). No missions, probe cards, objectives, recruiting, building or deploying.
officialBehaviour: Six steps: retrieve leaders, draw missions, launch probe droids, draw objective, advance time with recruit/build icons, deploy from the build queue (RR p.12, LTP p.10).
followUp: Refresh slice together with missions/objectives; needs the time track icon positions (DISC-018) and resource icon data.

title: No objectives; reputation never changes
engineBehaviour: Reputation stays at 14 for the whole game; the Rebel victory is reached only when time reaches 14.
officialBehaviour: The Rebels gain reputation from objective cards, moving the reputation marker toward the time marker (RR p.10, p.12; LTP p.11).
followUp: Objectives slice (needs combat and Refresh step 4).

title: No loyalty or subjugation (D-5, activation step 5)
engineBehaviour: D-5: no loyalty or subjugation markers exist; activation step 5 is skipped; first game loyalty markers are not placed.
officialBehaviour: Systems carry loyalty markers; an Imperial ground unit in a system without Imperial loyalty subjugates it at the end of an activation (RR p.2 step 5, p.8, p.13; LTP p.13).
followUp: Loyalty slice; it also feeds building, deployment and the permanent base reveal condition (DISC-009).

title: No voluntary base reveal (D-4)
engineBehaviour: D-4: the Rebel side has no command to reveal its base.
officialBehaviour: The Rebel player may reveal his base at the start of one of his Command Phase turns, before using a leader or passing (RR p.11; FAQ p.1 errata; not after passing, FAQ p.5).
followUp: Add a REVEAL_BASE command legal only at the start of a Rebel turn (combat on reveal comes with the combat slice).

title: The engine chooses the Rebel base (D-4, R-10)
engineBehaviour: R-10 / D-4: the base system is chosen by an FNV-1a hash of the game id among eligible systems: not Coruscant, not the five removed first game probe cards, not in or next to a system with starting Imperial units, and additionally not Bothawui (starting Rebel units).
officialBehaviour: The Rebel player secretly chooses the base from the probe deck (RR p.15 step 9); in the first game it must not hold or be adjacent to Imperial units (LTP p.5). A system with starting Rebel units such as Bothawui is allowed.
followUp: Let a human Rebel player choose the base during game setup; keep the Bothawui exclusion only while D-6 makes the base visible.

title: The "Rebel Base" space is merged with the base system (D-6)
engineBehaviour: D-6: units placed "on the base" stand in the base system (hidden from the Empire). Units there move like any others; a Rebel leader in the base system locks all of them; the space cannot be activated separately.
officialBehaviour: The "Rebel Base" space is not a system; units on it move to the base system or systems adjacent to it, the space can be activated from the base system or adjacent systems, and a leader on the space locks only the space (RR p.9-11, LTP p.12).
followUp: Model the space as its own location once deployment and voluntary reveal exist; revisit the Bothawui exclusion of DISC-007.

title: Base reveal checked only at the end of an Imperial activation (R-8, latent gap)
engineBehaviour: R-8: the base is revealed at FINISH_ACTIVATION of an Imperial activation of the base system when an Imperial ground unit is there. Within core-v1 this is equivalent, because Imperial ground units can only arrive by such an activation and loyalty does not exist.
officialBehaviour: Whenever the Empire has loyalty or ground units in the base system, the base must be revealed ("ever", RR p.11; LTP p.12); after movement it happens before combat (RR p.2 step 3).
followUp: Before adding loyalty, missions that move or place units, or deployment: make the reveal a state check run after every state change.

title: Fixed first game setup instead of standard setup (D-5, R-10)
engineBehaviour: D-5 / R-10: every game uses the LTP p.16 unit placement; loyalty markers, decks, action cards and the starting hand are not set up.
officialBehaviour: After the first game, step 8 uses random starting loyalty and free placement of starting units (RR p.15, LTP p.18).
followUp: Standard setup as a game option after loyalty and missions exist.

title: Only starting leaders; no Super Star Destroyer in play (D-7)
engineBehaviour: D-7: only the four starting leaders per side exist; recruitable leaders, action cards and the Super Star Destroyer never enter play.
officialBehaviour: Leaders are recruited at recruit icons of the time track (RR p.11-12); further units come from building (RR p.3).
followUp: Comes with the Refresh slice (recruiting) and building.

title: PASS is rejected during an own activation (interpretation, R-6)
engineBehaviour: R-6: PASS while the actor's activation is running returns activationInProgress; the player must FINISH_ACTIVATION first and may pass on a later turn.
officialBehaviour: RR p.6 lets a player pass "at any time during the Command Phase"; FAQ p.5 says a player passes instead of taking his turn. The engine follows the reading that a started activation is the turn.
followUp: Keep unless a ruling says otherwise; the entry is marked needs-review.

title: Transport capacity is checked within one MOVE_PIECES command (R-5, UX limit)
engineBehaviour: R-5: one MOVE_PIECES moves units from one source system; only ships moving in the same command provide capacity, so carried units must move together with their carriers.
officialBehaviour: Each moving ship brings ground units and TIE Fighters from its system up to its capacity; restricted units move only when carriers leave the same system (RR p.9, p.14). The rules do not split movement into commands.
followUp: UX only, no rules change needed: the UI and the AI must send carriers and their cargo in one command; reconsider if moves from one system are ever split into several steps.

title: Rebel faction sheet values are unconfirmed
engineBehaviour: core-v1 data uses capacities Corellian Corvette 2, Rebel Transport 4, Mon Calamari Cruiser 4 (and no attack/health) taken from a fan data set; Imperial values were read from the faction sheet illustration.
officialBehaviour: Capacity, attack and health are printed on the faction sheets (RR p.3, p.8, p.14); the Rebel sheet values are not in the rules text.
followUp: Product owner checks the Rebel faction sheet; correct the data in src/scenario/core/catalog.ts if different (no rules code change).

title: Component limitations are not modelled (n/a in the slice)
engineBehaviour: No unit, leader or marker is ever created, so limits cannot be reached and are not checked.
officialBehaviour: Units, leaders and rings are limited to the box contents; dice are capped at five per colour; markers are unlimited (RR p.6).
followUp: Enforce unit limits together with building (Refresh slice) and dice caps with combat.

title: Map data: Mustafar–Utapau adjacency and region names unconfirmed
engineBehaviour: core-v1 treats Mustafar and Utapau as not adjacent and uses region ids r1..r8 with unofficial labels; the 69 adjacency edges come from cross-checked fan data.
officialBehaviour: Adjacency is defined by shared borders and impassable areas on the board (RR p.9, p.12); the rules give no region names.
followUp: Product owner checks the Mustafar–Utapau border and whether the board prints region names; data fix only.

title: Leader data: which leaders lack tactic values
engineBehaviour: core-v1 marks Mon Mothma as the only starting leader that cannot activate (canActivate false), from fan data.
officialBehaviour: A leader without tactic values cannot activate a system (RR p.2, p.9); tactic values are printed on the leader tokens.
followUp: Product owner checks the starting leader tokens (and later the recruitable ones).

title: Time track recruit/build icon positions unknown
engineBehaviour: core-v1 does not use the icons (no recruiting or building); the positions are known only with low confidence.
officialBehaviour: Recruit and build happen when the time marker enters a space showing those icons (RR p.12, LTP p.10).
followUp: Read the icon positions from the board before the Refresh slice.
